title: NetworkError and stricter retries
summary: Ky now wraps fetch network failures in a typed NetworkError. It retries only errors it knows, and throws everything else at once.

links.title: Issue #545: Best way to handle fetch errors
PR #842: why the detector is inlined

steps.title: Ky retried bugs like network failures
steps.body:
- When the network fails, fetch rejects with a plain `TypeError`.
- The message differs per runtime: `Failed to fetch` in Chrome, `fetch failed` in Node.js, `Load failed` in Safari.
- Callers could not tell a network failure from a bug.
- On a retriable method, Ky retried every error that the fetch call threw.
- A bug in a custom `fetch` got retries with backoff, like a network failure (#545).

links.title: Issue #545: Best way to handle fetch errors

steps.title: Retry only errors Ky recognizes
steps.body:
- `#fetch` wraps a fetch `TypeError` with a known network message in the new `NetworkError`. The original `TypeError` stays in `cause`.
- By default, Ky retries only `HTTPError`, `TimeoutError`, `NetworkError` and `ForceRetryError`. It throws any other error at once.
- sindresorhus picked this allowlist over a denylist of known non-retriable errors. A runtime with an unknown message gets no retries: "New runtimes don't come along every day."
- `shouldRetry` can still force a retry of any error. The readme points to it for unrecognized runtimes.
- Ky copies `is-network-error` into its own source. Ky stays a package with no dependencies.

links.title: #545: the proposal, wrap and allowlist or denylist

terms.meaning: The new `KyError` subclass that `#fetch` throws in place of a raw network error.
A fetch `TypeError` whose message `isRawNetworkError` finds in a list of known runtime messages, such as `Failed to fetch` or `fetch failed`.
The exported type guard that returns true for a `NetworkError` instance or for any error whose `name` is `NetworkError`.
The standard error property where `NetworkError` keeps the raw network error that fetch rejected with.
The method that gets each failed attempt's error and returns a delay to retry, or throws the error to stop.
A user callback that returns `true` to force a retry, `false` to stop, or `undefined` to use the default rules.
An HTTP method that Ky may retry, by default `get`, `put`, `head`, `delete`, `options` and `trace`, so not `post` or `patch`.
The largest number of retries after the first attempt, 2 by default.

steps.title: The request path
steps.say: Every Ky attempt runs through `#fetch`. The PR wraps network failures there in `NetworkError`. It also ends the retry decision with a check for `NetworkError`.

notes.text: `Ky.create` runs every request through `#retry`. Each attempt calls `#fetch`. Only `#fetch` calls `options.fetch`.
When `options.fetch` rejects, `#fetch` asks `isRawNetworkError` whether the error is a raw network error. On a match, `#fetch` throws a `NetworkError`. `#fetch` rethrows any other error unchanged.

`#retry` passes each error through `#retryFromError` to the retry decision, `#calculateRetryDelay`. The retry decision asks `shouldRetry` when the caller set one. A returned delay means Ky waits, then starts another attempt.

steps.title: One network failure, then success
steps.say: A GET fails once with `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`, then succeeds. Ky wraps the failure in a `NetworkError` and retries. The caller gets the second response.

messages.label: TypeError: Failed to fetch
messages.note: `isRawNetworkError` recognizes this message as a raw network error.

messages.label: delay (ms)
messages.note: GET is a retriable method. The error is a `NetworkError`, so the retry decision returns a delay.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: What happens when a GET with a retry limit of 2 uses a custom `fetch` that always throws `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`?

options.text: Ky calls `fetch` 3 times. The caller catches a `NetworkError` with the `TypeError` in `cause`.
options.why: Each failure becomes a `NetworkError`, which the retry decision retries twice on a GET before it throws.

options.text: Ky calls `fetch` 3 times. The caller catches the raw `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`.
options.why: `#fetch` wraps the last failure too, so the caller gets a `NetworkError`, not the raw `TypeError`.

options.text: Ky calls `fetch` once. The caller catches the raw `TypeError`, because Ky throws unknown errors at once.
options.why: `isRawNetworkError` recognizes `Failed to fetch` from a custom `fetch` too, so the error is a `NetworkError` and gets retried.

options.text: Ky calls `fetch` 2 times. The caller catches a `NetworkError` with the `TypeError` in `cause`.
options.why: The retry limit counts retries after the first attempt, so a limit of 2 gives 3 calls.

steps.title: A typed error for network failures
steps.say: `NetworkError` is the new error that Ky throws when fetch fails at the network level. `isNetworkError` recognizes it. `isKyError` now counts it as a Ky error.

notes.text: `NetworkError` copies the shape of `TimeoutError`: a `KyError` subclass with a `request` property and a message with the method and URL. The constructor passes the raw fetch error to the standard `cause` option.
`isNetworkError` matches an `instanceof` check or the `name` `'NetworkError'`, like `isHTTPError` above it. The `name` check recognizes an error from another realm or another copy of Ky.
`isKyError` now also returns `true` for a `NetworkError`. Before, a network failure was a raw `TypeError`, so `isKyError` returned `false` for it.

steps.title: A fetch failure becomes a NetworkError
steps.say: `#fetch` now catches every rejection from the fetch call. A raw network error leaves `#fetch` as a `NetworkError`.

notes.text: This file is an inlined copy of `is-network-error` v1.3.1. `isRawNetworkError` returns `true` only for a `TypeError` whose message a known runtime uses for a network failure, such as `fetch failed` from undici.

The `try` covers both fetch paths: the direct call when `timeout` is `false`, and the `timeout()` race. Both paths now use `return await`, so a rejection lands in this `catch`. Before, they returned the promise without `await`.
The `catch` wraps a raw network error in a `NetworkError` and passes the raw error as `cause`.
undici rejects this request with `TypeError('fetch failed')`, so Ky now wraps that `TypeError`. The undici code moves one level deeper, to `error.cause.cause.code`.

steps.title: Retry decision ends in an allowlist
steps.say: `#calculateRetryDelay` still checks the retry limit, `ForceRetryError`, the retriable method and `shouldRetry` first, in that order. After them, each known error type now returns its own delay.

notes.text: The timeout branch now returns its own delay when `retryOnTimeout` is on. Before, a `TimeoutError` fell through to one shared `return` at the end of the method. That `return` now sits behind the `NetworkError` check, so the branch needs its own.
The HTTP branch ends with the same explicit `return`, for the same reason.
Only a `NetworkError` gets a delay here. `#calculateRetryDelay` throws any other error at once, with no retry.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: What happens when a POST's fetch rejects with `TypeError('Failed to fetch')` and the retry limit is 2?

options.text: Fetch runs once, and the caller catches a `NetworkError`.
options.why: `#fetch` wraps the error, then the retriable method check throws it because POST is not in the default `retry.methods`.

options.text: Fetch runs 3 times, and the caller catches a `NetworkError`.
options.why: The retriable method check runs before the type check, so a POST gets no retry.

options.text: Fetch runs once, and the caller catches the raw `TypeError`.
options.why: `#fetch` wraps a recognized `TypeError` before the retry decision runs, so the caller gets a `NetworkError`.

options.text: Fetch runs 3 times, and the caller catches the raw `TypeError`.
options.why: `#fetch` wraps the recognized `TypeError`, and the method check stops any retry for POST.

steps.title: A bug fails on the first try
steps.say: A `TypeError` with an unknown message, such as a bug in a custom `fetch`, fails on the first attempt. The retry decision throws it, because it is not a `NetworkError`.

notes.text: An error that `isRawNetworkError` does not recognize leaves the catch unchanged. A bug `TypeError`, a `TimeoutError` or an `AbortError` reaches the retry decision with its own type.
The custom `fetch` throws `TypeError('Cannot read properties of undefined')` with retry limit 2. Ky calls `fetch` exactly once. The caller catches a `TypeError`.

steps.title: The user can still force retries
steps.say: `isRawNetworkError` knows a fixed set of runtime messages. For any other error, `shouldRetry` is the way to get retries back.

notes.text: `#fetch` wraps the error before the retry decision calls `shouldRetry`. The test checks that `shouldRetry` gets a `NetworkError` with the raw `TypeError` in `cause`.
`shouldRetry: () => true` makes the retry decision return a delay before its type checks run. A bug `TypeError('Cannot read properties of undefined')` gets 3 fetch calls with retry limit 2.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: What happens when a custom `fetch` on a GET throws `new Error('socket hang up')` with default retry options?

options.text: Ky calls `fetch` once, and the caller catches the original `Error`.
options.why: `#fetch` leaves an error named `Error` unwrapped, so the retry decision throws it at once.

options.text: Ky wraps it in a `NetworkError` and retries it up to the retry limit.
options.why: `isRawNetworkError` accepts only errors named `TypeError`, so Ky does not wrap this one.

options.text: Ky retries the raw `Error` up to the retry limit, because GET is retriable.
options.why: Without a `shouldRetry` that returns `true`, the retry decision throws any error of an unknown type.

options.text: Ky calls `fetch` once, and the caller catches a `NetworkError` with the `Error` in `cause`.
options.why: Only a `TypeError` with a known message gets wrapped, so the caller sees the original `Error`.

steps.title: What to check
steps.body:
- The PR does not say if this ships as a breaking change. Code that checks `instanceof TypeError`, matches `'Failed to fetch'` or reads `error.cause.code` no longer matches. The `is-network-error` package returns `false` for a `NetworkError`, so the #545 `beforeRetry` workaround may stop retries.
- A network failure with an unknown message is no longer retried. Examples are a custom `fetch`, a polyfill, or a browser that changes its message. Nothing warns the user.
- undici uses `fetch failed` for client bugs too, such as a content-length mismatch or an `invalid:` URL. Ky wraps them in `NetworkError`. A GET retries them with backoff. The readme says that programming bugs are thrown immediately.
- `isNetworkError` and `isKyError` accept any error named `NetworkError`. `DOMException` uses that name too. A foreign error with that name has no `request`. The retry decision still retries it like a real `NetworkError`.
- `#fetch` wraps only the fetch call. If the connection drops while `.json()` reads the body, the caller gets a raw `TypeError` with no retry. This includes undici's `terminated`, which is in the message set.

steps.title: Also changed
steps.body:
- `readme.md` documents the new retry policy and adds a `NetworkError` section. The hook and error docs now name `NetworkError`.
- `source/index.ts` exports `NetworkError` and `isNetworkError`.
- Doc comments change in `source/types/options.ts`, `source/types/retry.ts`, `source/types/hooks.ts`, `source/errors/KyError.ts` and `source/errors/HTTPError.ts`. The retry docs drop the stale line "Retries are not triggered following a timeout".
- `test/hooks.ts` and `test/memory-leak.ts` now expect a `NetworkError`. The fake fetch failures in `test/hooks.ts` throw `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`. Most old fake errors do not match `isRawNetworkError`, so Ky would throw them before `beforeRetry` runs.
- Other new tests in `test/retry.ts` check the `NetworkError` shape, the default retry, POST and `timeout: false`. They also check `shouldRetry` returning `undefined`, `beforeError`, and a non-network `TypeError` that stays unwrapped.
